about: A story as a small graph: claims, each with its label, who said it, when, and the rows and data fields that support it. The page is generated from this file by tools/stories-build.mjs; nothing here is new reporting. See stories/grammar.md. Every "nothing announced" here is a tripwire: its support expects the board card to be open or the decision edge to be not_announced, so the check fails, and the sentence is retold, when an answer arrives.
title: What nobody has said yet
standfirst: Day 2 is off and the storm has its warnings. What has no answer on Wednesday morning: whether Day 3 runs (the press reported it confirmed early on Wednesday afternoon; not read at the organisers' own page), what becomes of the lost day's talks, the PITCH semi-final, the side events and the tickets, and where the government's advice is written down. Each line here is an absence, with when and where it was last looked for.

warnings_in_force.about: The official warnings a story about the storm states first, drawn as the front page draws them: for each kind of weather IPMA's newest message by the time it was sent (cap.json beside this file), saying what IPMA's open-data feed (this file) lists where the two differ; resolved when the page is built and read again in the reader's browser. Never a level of our own.

sections.title: The city and its transport on Thursday

claims.text: At 19:09 on Tuesday Web Summit said Day 2 "will not take place", and gave one sentence on everything that follows from it: "Web Summit will communicate directly with those impacted."
claims.label: fact

contains: Day 2 (Wednesday, November 11th) will not take place
Web Summit will communicate directly with those impacted

claims.text: On Thursday the same page gives an aim and a promise of more: "Web Summit aims to proceed with Day 3 (Thursday, November 12) as planned", with "further updates as soon as confirmed information becomes available".
claims.label: fact

contains: further updates as soon as confirmed information becomes available

claims.text: Does Day 3 go ahead? The press now says yes, relaying the organisers: 24 Notícias (read 13:04) reports that Web Summit told participants on Wednesday it reopens on Thursday 12 November for its last day, with part of Wednesday's programme moved to Thursday, and Público's caption (12:17) has the arena and FIL reopening on Thursday, "confirma a organização". Neither says it read the organisers' own text, the organisers' page is not read here (its terms forbid automated reading), and their public accounts have posted nothing since Tuesday 17:36. Reported, not read at source; the card stays open on the board.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: 24 Notícias and Público, relaying the organisers' message to participants

claims.text: What happens to Wednesday's talks and speakers? Whether they are cancelled, moved to Thursday or put online has not been published anywhere this site can read.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: incident.researcher@web-summit.dinis, the decision graph (an absence, as read)

claims.text: One sign from outside the organisers: at 21:41 on Tuesday a speaker said in public that Day 2 was cancelled and that his talks and press conference stayed on Thursday. A speaker's account is evidence; it settles nothing for anyone else.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: a speaker, in public (as the timeline has it)

claims.text: Where and when does the PITCH semi-final run? Its session page still read "November 11, 2026 • 5.00PM - 6.00PM Centre Stage" when read at 02:55 on Wednesday, with no word of the storm: a slot on a day that will not take place. No new day, time or place has been announced.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: Web Summit's schedule pages, as read; incident.researcher@web-summit.dinis, the decision graph (an absence, as read)

claims.text: What happens to Wednesday's side events? Web Summit's own Night Summit was still listed for Wednesday evening, with no notice, when its page was last read at 01:36; one side event's own page showed no notice either.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: incident.researcher@web-summit.dinis, the decision graph (an absence, as read)

claims.text: The government's order for Wednesday suspends outdoor events and does not mention Web Summit or its side events: Despacho n.º 13773-A/2026, in force from 00:00 to 23:59 on 11 November.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: the Government of Portugal, Diário da República (Despacho n.º 13773-A/2026)

claims.text: What do ticket holders get for the lost day? No Web Summit page said anything about tickets, refunds or compensation when last read.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: incident.researcher@web-summit.dinis, the decision graph (an absence, as read)

claims.text: The press had no more: the international reports of the cancellation on Tuesday evening carried nothing on refunds or on PITCH.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: the international press, as the timeline has it

claims.text: Where is the government's advice, as a text? The organisers wrote that the government had "formally advised" against Day 2. The recommendation itself is known only as a press live blog reported it at 17:53, and the order read at source does not carry it: "formally advised" has no legal text and stays the organisers' own wording.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: incident.researcher@web-summit.dinis, reading the Diário da República; the recommendation is evidence (Jornal de Negócios' live blog)

claims.text: Thursday's transport: no notice for Thursday from the Metro, Carris, CP, the ferries or the bridges was found when the operators' sites were read late on Tuesday and again at 00:33 on Wednesday.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: incident.researcher@web-summit.dinis, the decision graph (an absence, as read)

claims.text: The nearest thing to a word on Thursday from the government is an expectation, not a service decision: Lusa (14:46) and CNN Portugal's live page (14:44) report the Interior Minister saying the alert situation ends at midnight as planned and that the government expects normality to resume on Thursday, with repair work. That agrees with the government's order, which declared the alert for 00:00 to 23:59 on 11 November. Reported by the press, not read at the government's own pages.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: Lusa and CNN Portugal, relaying the Interior Minister

claims.text: The city's own measures: a page titled "Situação de Alerta: medidas excecionais em Lisboa" was seen in a search, but the city's site refuses automated reads, so what it says is not in the data room. A person must read it.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: incident.researcher@web-summit.dinis, the decision graph (a page seen by its title, not read)

claims.text: These absences are read from further away than they were. Since 05:25 on Wednesday no agent of this site reads websummit.com: its terms forbid automated access, and the hold stands until Dinis Cruz decides. Our last read of it was 04:33. An answer now reaches us through a person, the press or the organisers' public accounts, and still counts as answered only from the organisers' own channel.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: incident.conductor@web-summit.dinis (the hold); incident.sources@web-summit.dinis (the terms, as read)

contains: Our last read of websummit.com was 04:33Z
it still counts as answered only from the organisers' own channel

claims.text: The last answer was missed for more than an hour while every page we watched was being read: the decision on Day 2 went up at 19:09 in the organisers' blog, outside the list we watched, and was seen at 20:58..
claims.label: fact

contains: we watched the sitemap, home and /news/ and saw it only at 20:58

not_known.text: What would close the question of Day 3: a Web Summit page after the storm that confirms Thursday, or changes it.
What would close the question of the talks: a Web Summit page, or its official account, saying what happens to Day 2's programme. A press report or one speaker's post moves nothing.
What would close PITCH: a Web Summit page giving the semi-final's day, time and place after the closure.
What would close the side events: for Night Summit, a Web Summit page saying it is off, moved or on; for any other, its own organiser's page.
What would close tickets: a Web Summit page, or its terms as the organiser points to them, stating what ticket holders get for Day 2.
What would close the advice: the text on a government channel, or the government saying on the record that it was given by word only.
Whether any of this has been said directly to those affected (by email or in the event's app): the organisers said they would "communicate directly", and nothing sent directly is in the data room.
